variants.label: Mobile — header, search and chat
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity MOBILE responsive adaptation of the supplied approved desktop Pets4Luv homepage. This is the SAME website, not a redesign. Output a single narrow portrait mobile website screenshot at approximately 390 CSS pixels wide rendered at high resolution, about 1024px wide by 2560px tall. No phone hardware, browser chrome, presentation margins or desktop layout. Comfortable mobile text sizes (body around 16px equivalent, controls minimum 44px tall), 20px side padding, no horizontal overflow. Preserve exact red-heart Pets4Luv logo artwork, warm ivory background, deep burgundy accents, elegant serif storytelling headlines, clean upright sans-serif UI/body, thin fine borders, NO search panel shadow. This output is one of two consecutive scroll views of the same mobile page; do not compress the whole desktop page into this one screen. Maintain mature warm editorial style. Realistic animal photography from reference.
FIRST SCROLL VIEW: Show the top of the mobile page through the end of the integrated chat section. Do not include weekly animal cards in this view.
Compact white mobile masthead about 72 CSS px tall: exact small heart logo at left, modest burgundy Donate button and an accessible 'Menu' hamburger control at right. Desktop nav links collapse into the closed Menu (do not show desktop nav row).
Hero immediately below: same senior golden dog and tabby cat lying directly together on blanket. Adapt crop for mobile by putting large cream SERIF motto 'Bringing families together' in the dark top-left/top third over soft photographic background, and smaller UPRIGHT SANS subtitle 'One rescue at a time'. Both animal faces must appear fully visible side-by-side across the lower two-thirds, neither cut off nor covered by text. Warm sunlit photographic style, no hero CTA button. Hero about 350 CSS px tall.
Below, a thin-bordered ivory search/chat panel with no shadow, comfortable spacing and 16px inner padding. Bold sans burgundy heading 'Find your furry best friend' wraps to two lines; below it 'View all animals →' link. Full-width three-segment selector 'All pets' / 'Cats' / 'Dogs', All pets selected burgundy. Next row two equal width dropdown fields with labels AGE / SIZE, values Any age / Any size. Under them full-width burgundy button 'Show matching pets →'. Then a QUIET regular small warm-gray divider phrase 'OR tell us what you’re looking for', wrapping neatly to two lines if necessary, flanked by short thin pale rules. Under divider burgundy chat icon plus semibold 'Ask Pets4Luv'. Full-width WHITE MULTILINE message textarea with placeholder EXACTLY 'Tell us about your ideal companion', natural wrap to two lines, at least 80 CSS px high. Put visible burgundy Send button in a separate bottom-right row beneath the textarea, not covering placeholder. Then regular sans helper text 'You can also ask about adoption, pet care, or volunteering.' wrapping naturally. Panel ends here; slight ivory margin at bottom. The chat composer is visible so do not overlay a floating launcher over it in this screenshot. Keep typography comfortably readable and enough vertical space; tall scrolling capture is fine. ALL these elements must be shown; do not drop chat or filter labels. No fake chat conversation or result counts.

variants.label: Mobile — weekly highlights
variants.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a high-fidelity MOBILE responsive adaptation of the supplied approved desktop Pets4Luv homepage. This is the SAME website, not a redesign. Output a single narrow portrait mobile website screenshot at approximately 390 CSS pixels wide rendered at high resolution, about 1024px wide by 2560px tall. No phone hardware, browser chrome, presentation margins or desktop layout. Comfortable mobile text sizes (body around 16px equivalent, controls minimum 44px tall), 20px side padding, no horizontal overflow. Preserve exact red-heart Pets4Luv logo artwork, warm ivory background, deep burgundy accents, elegant serif storytelling headlines, clean upright sans-serif UI/body, thin fine borders, NO search panel shadow. This output is one of two consecutive scroll views of the same mobile page; do not compress the whole desktop page into this one screen. Maintain mature warm editorial style. Realistic animal photography from reference.
SECOND SCROLL VIEW: This shows the next section of the SAME mobile page, immediately after the search/chat panel in the first view. Start with weekly highlights; NO repeated masthead, hero, search, chat form or filter panel.
Top 20px margin then compact burgundy uppercase sans label 'FEATURED ANIMALS OF THE WEEK'. Next large elegant serif headline 'Some love stories take a little longer.' wrapping naturally to three lines. Next regular sans copy 'Each week, we highlight a few adoptable pets who are ready for their next chapter — and a home to call their own.' readable natural wrap.
Below introduce Luna with the same large tabby photograph as desktop, full content width 350 CSS px, crop about 4:3 or square. Beneath image burgundy caption area in upright sans. Left 'Luna' and smaller 'This week’s spotlight' stacked, right clear white underlined 'Meet Luna →' with comfortable tap spacing. No collisions.
Then two STACKED compact horizontal animal story cards, each with photo left around 105px wide and text right. First Milo's same happy dog portrait, heading 'Meet Milo' bold burgundy sans, description 'A friendly, affectionate pup who loves people and playtime.', clear 'See Milo →'. Second Olive's same cat portrait, heading 'Meet Olive', description 'A gentle, curious cat who’s ready to be someone’s best friend.', clear 'See Olive →'. Thin warm separators, generous vertical spacing, all copy readable, no tiny desktop type.
Bottom footer in small upright sans: 'Design concept • Sample animals'. Show a burgundy rounded floating-style 'Ask Pets4Luv' launcher with speech icon near bottom-right but place it in RESERVED clear space below the last animal story so it never obscures any photo, copy or link. Add enough footer bottom space for the launcher. No new sections, no new animal names, no stats or forms. This is the lower-page mobile continuation, not a standalone landing page.
